zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 6; they obstruct downward and outward views from Decks 6, 9, and 10, with Deck 6 most affected.
zones.effect: Oceanview and balcony cabins on these decks look directly at or over orange lifeboat tops instead of clean water views; the horizon remains visible above the boats.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to guests prioritizing unobstructed ocean views or photography; doesn't matter to those focused on having a balcony for air and space rather than the vista, or to anyone in an interior cabin.

zones.what: The Dome (multi-story entertainment venue) sits directly below the midship section of Deck 9.
zones.effect: Evening entertainment noise and vibration from live shows and performances may be noticeable in cabins directly above, particularly during peak evening hours.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers and early-to-bed travelers; doesn't matter to those who stay out late or aren't noise-sensitive.

zones.what: Main dining rooms and galley operations sit directly below the aft section of Deck 10.
zones.effect: Matters to light sleepers and those sensitive to mechanical hums or service activity sounds; doesn't matter to sound sleepers or those rarely in their cabin during meal times.

zones.what: The Dome upper levels and the Pool Deck sit directly above midship and aft Deck 16.
zones.effect: Daytime pool deck activity, furniture dragging, and evening entertainment noise may be audible; foot traffic and music from the pool bar can carry through until late evening.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to those wanting quiet during the day or early evenings; doesn't matter to heavy sleepers or guests who prefer the energy of being near the action.

zones.what: The World Fresh Marketplace (buffet) operates directly above portions of midship and aft Deck 15.
zones.effect: Early morning buffet prep (starting around 6 AM), foot traffic, chair movement, and service activity throughout breakfast and lunch hours create noise overhead.
zones.mattersTo: Matters significantly to late sleepers and those sensitive to early morning noise; doesn't matter to early risers or those planning to be at breakfast anyway.

zones.what: Aft cabins on the lowest guest decks sit closest to propulsion machinery and stabilizer mechanisms.
zones.effect: Low-frequency vibration and mechanical hum are most noticeable here, particularly during maneuvering, rough seas, or when stabilizers are active.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to vibration-sensitive guests and light sleepers; doesn't matter to those unbothered by background hum or who use white noise anyway.

zones.what: Forward cabins on lower decks experience bow thruster noise during docking and maneuvering, plus anchor chain deployment in port.
zones.effect: Loud mechanical rumble during docking (usually early morning arrival) and anchor operations; the sound is brief but can be jarring if asleep.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to light sleepers on port days with early arrival times; doesn't matter to heavy sleepers or early risers who'll be up anyway.

zones.what: Elevator and stair banks are positioned forward, midship, and aft on all cabin decks, with midship banks serving the highest traffic.
zones.effect: Cabins immediately adjacent to elevator lobbies experience door chimes, conversation, and foot traffic throughout the night; midship elevators are busiest due to main dining room and atrium access.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers and those sensitive to hallway noise; doesn't matter to sound sleepers or those who prioritize convenience over quiet.
